primary_metric: Debian popcon sourcemax installations by source package (pinned snapshot)
uncertainty: One verified C++ SQL path after the shared Debian popcon source-name search (names containing 'sql', first 100 of 229 by rank) plus round-2 targeted lookups in the same pinned snapshot (duckdb, hsql/hyrise, gdal, kdb, libreoffice, sqlitebrowser, sqlitestudio, antlr4-cpp-runtime, soci, poco). DuckDB 2.0.0 (Debian source duckdb, 40 installations) parses both valid controls with its built-in PEG grammar through duckdb::Parser, without a database or client context, into SQLStatement trees that give the oracle summary; the adapter reports DuckDB's count_star node for COUNT(*) as count. Higher-ranked C++ sources are wrappers, applications with internal parsers, a runtime without a grammar, or parsers that cannot read the INSERT control or need a connection (GDAL OGR SQL, KDb). hsql has a documented AST API but no Debian source package in the pinned snapshot and no Debian development package to use as the fallback, so it has no admissible metric. Round 3 (2026-11-18) checked further sources of the same snapshot (qgis: QgsSQLStatement has no GROUP BY or INSERT; futuresql: asynchronous QtSql wrapper without a parser), with evidence in leads.json. No other C++ source package in the snapshot has a documented SQL syntax-tree API, so after round 3 the cell stopped at one path; GitHub stars were then allowed only in PLY cells. The popcon count is very small and counts installs of the whole engine, not use of its parser. DuckDB's parser is a public header of an engine whose C++ API is described upstream as internal. Two valid controls establish only the tested dialect-neutral subset. Round 4 (2026-11-18) found no second path. Further snapshot lookups (mysql-9.7, firebird4.0, firebird3.0, apache-arrow, mysql-connector-c++, sqlsmith, usql) are servers or engines with internal grammars, libraries without an SQL parser, a query generator, and a Go client that only shares the usql name. vcpkg and Conan Center list C++ SQL builders, ORMs, wrappers and clients but no SQL parser library. The GitHub search 'sql parser language:C++' (discovery only) and the task's named leads give C++ parsers without a Debian, vcpkg or Conan package and therefore without an admissible metric: cybergarage/usql, sqltoast and GoogleSQL (ZetaSQL), recorded as unresolved_no_primary_metric next to hsql; ClickHouse's parser is internal to its server. After round 4 the cell stopped at one path. Round 6 (2026-11-18) applied the C and C++ GitHub-star fallback: a tagged upstream release of a format-specific parser repository with at least 100 stars may fill slots left after the popcon path, ranked separately and never compared with popcon counts. GoogleSQL 2026.11.2 (google/googlesql, formerly google/zetasql; 2,642 stars, Apache-2.0) parses both valid controls with googlesql::ParseNextStatement and default LanguageOptions into an AST that gives the oracle summary. Its stars cover the whole GoogleSQL repository (parser, analyzer, reference implementation, Java and Go front ends), not installs or parser use; upstream calls the parser API semi-public because parse trees are not stable. The other round-6 candidates do not qualify: hsql (hyrise/sql-parser, 813 stars) has no tag or release; sqlcheck is a regex anti-pattern checker; SQLines and constexpr-sql have no tag; cybergarage/usql (55) and sqltoast (33) are below 100 stars. The cell stops at two paths, not ten.
